title: Connectivity and Diameter of Friends and Strangers Graphs Using Minimum Degree
summary: Given graphs $X,Y$ on $n$ vertices, Defant and Kravitz defined the friends and strangers graph, denoted $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$. The vertices of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ are bijections $σ:V(X)\to V(Y)$, and two bijections $σ$ and $σ'$ are adjacent in $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ if they differ by a transposition $(ab)$ such that $a$ and $b$ are adjacent in $X$ and $σ(a)$ and $σ(b)$ are adjacent in $Y$. Our main result resolves a conjecture of Bangachev that if $X,Y$ are connected graphs and $2\min\{δ(X),δ(Y)\}+3\max\{δ(X),δ(Y)\}\ge 3n$, then $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ is connected.
